name: ${name}
description: Tactical nuclear devices for Minecraft: a four-preset device with a real arming flow, and a detonation that is staged rather than faked — blinding flash, fireball, shockwave rings, a procedural mushroom cloud, cratering, drifting fallout with radiation sickness, and an EMP that silences machines in a bounded zone. Every visual system is fed by one compact server event, so a 50-megaton detonation costs the server a handful of block writes per tick and nothing at all when nothing is armed.
credits: Built as a demonstration of staged, server-authoritative effect design on Fabric.
_comment: The three placeholders above (id, version, name) are expanded by processResources in build.gradle
from gradle.properties (mod_id / mod_version / mod_name), so the manifest can never disagree with
the jar it ships inside. That expansion is a Groovy template, which is the one reason this file may
not contain a dollar sign followed by an open brace, or a trailing backslash, even in a comment: the
template engine parses it anyway and the build dies in processResources pointing at no file at all.
'depends' on fabric-api rather than on the individual modules: the mod uses the networking,
rendering (HUD + entity renderers), command, object-builder and lifecycle-API modules, and an
aggregate dependency states that plainly. A user installing a partial fabric-api is not a case
worth breaking the mod for — the loader reports the missing module at startup either way.
'suggests' modmenu is informational: the config screen is reachable without it through
/doomsday config, which is why the entrypoint class is loaded reflectively by Mod Menu only.
No 'breaks' entries: nothing here rewrites a vanilla class, and the single mixin targets
GameRenderer at TAIL in two methods that no other mod is known to replace outright.
minecraft is pinned with '~' (1.21.x patch flow) rather than '>=1.21.1': the mixin selectors, the
TypedActionResult signature and the blockstate/model schema this jar ships were checked against
1.21.1 mappings specifically, so a newer patch that changes them should refuse to load rather than
load and crash on the first detonation.
